Estimate relic abundances through misalignment, thermally suppressed production, strong-interaction freeze-out, effective-operator decays and glueball entropy dilution. Conditional monopole abundances use Kibble or Kibble–Zurek estimates, followed by annihilation and dilution.

Integrate out ψ using heat-kernel methods, then use a local metric redefinition to expose derivative contact interactions. Match the resulting EFT amplitude to direct one-loop calculations using Feynman parameters, dimensional regularization and LSZ wavefunction factors; field redefinitions leave scattering amplitudes invariant.

Use fixed-t dispersion relations, optical-theorem positivity and improved bounds that subtract known positive intermediate-state contributions. Analyze compactified amplitudes through KK sums and examine their infrared behavior using graviton-mass regulation, partial waves and eikonal resummation.

Integrate the differential event rate over lens distance, event duration and the normalized M31 stellar-radius distribution. The adopted radius distribution comes from a cited PHAT-catalogue/MIST analysis; expected counts are converted to Poisson upper limits on fDM.

Project lens mass onto the lens plane and solve ū(φ)=t(φ)−m(t(φ))/t(φ) for image boundaries. Integrate image areas with their parity factors and sum magnifications; iteratively find the threshold impact parameter for each lens/source size.
Resolve tangent and normal bundles before expanding. Choose characters according to the representation, account for normal-spinor multiplicity, and then apply the Majorana-Weyl reality factor.

Extract a geometric factorization of I₈ from massless RR tadpole exchange and D-brane/O-plane tensor couplings. Compare geometric and integral charge bases; use T-dual intersecting-brane intersection numbers to describe anomaly lattices and wrapped-brane charges.

Replace representation traces before summing anomalies. For product representations, expand F_m⊗1+1⊗F_n; this explains the dimension factors, mixed quartic coefficient, and omitted terms when traces are nonzero.

Compute defect spectra from open-string amplitudes and match their anomalies to inflow: I₄=(Q·a/2)trR²+Σᵢ[Q·bᵢ/(2λᵢ)]trFᵢ²+(Q·Q/2)χ(N). This determines charge products and permits comparison with central charges and current-algebra bounds.
Select the characteristic class for each chiral field, expand to the necessary form degree, multiply, and extract the anomaly form. Apply the appropriate chirality sign and reality factor.
Factorize the six-dimensional anomaly polynomial, identify anomaly vectors, and impose the simultaneous conditions on J. The decisive inequalities are equation (72), outside this window.

Project the open-string amplitudes, combine the specified surfaces, and extract massless character coefficients. This gives representation multiplicities and chirality, rather than estimating the spectrum from charge data alone.

Translate finite magnetic fields into wrapping data, evaluate intersections, and apply the chosen projection. Zero-denominator wrapping descriptions remain separate, and formal table coefficients require a further physical-admissibility check.

Match bulk inflow to worldsheet anomalies and apply conformal consistency conditions. The paper tests this operation against explicit orientifold spectra; its complete inequalities are equation (12), outside the supplied window.

Use SU(N) index counting and N-ality to identify an accidental hidden baryon number; inspect gauge-invariant operators for explicit breaking, minimize the renormalizable Higgs potential and obtain the axion coupling from anomalous fermions.

Estimate quadratic radiative corrections to the PQ Higgs mass and compare them with its symmetry-breaking scale. Adopt tower state counting and the gravitational species bound to estimate a quantum-gravity cutoff, then identify that scale with the field-theory cutoff.
Rewrite the background equations using first-order scalar functions W,S,T, match UV and acceptable IR asymptotics, and integrate numerically for explicit steep and soft potentials.

Construct gauge-invariant fluctuations and radial Schrödinger eigenvalue problems. Spin-0 fluctuations form a coupled doublet; the tensor equation is separate. Rotations remove first radial derivatives, A is used as a numerical coordinate, and WKB estimates high-excitation spectra.

Obtain the cubic action by adapting and analytically continuing an imported multifield-inflation calculation, then integrate radial wave-function overlaps. Numerical CP tests focus on couplings without boundary-coordinate derivatives.

Insert a volume-dependent metric into the ten-dimensional action, integrate the internal space, and select coefficients giving Einstein gravity and canonical scalars. Analyze stationary equations and Hessians of the resulting potential.
Integrate warped probe-string tension along the transverse direction and match it to a particle action using the induced endpoint metric.

Reduce the product metric, impose a constant external gravitational prefactor, discard a total derivative, and normalize the radion kinetic term. This fixes conventions for comparing potential terms. The derivation uses the starting metric because the printed intermediate curvature formula has unresolved coefficients.
Integrate out the top form with its boundary term, retain the discontinuity sourced by the membrane, and identify the resulting energy with the flux contribution.
Choose a product and flux frame, eliminate flux density using its integral, solve for the constant dilaton, and test both curvature equations for positive radii.

Trace the external Einstein equation, compare warp-derivative coefficients with an exponential Laplacian, and integrate over the internal manifold. Here the literal equation fails the cancellation test. A total-Laplacian route is available only under the explicitly proposed coefficient reconstruction and compatible source conventions.

Starting conditionally from Eq. (7.6), expand the spherical jump equation, extract a Friedmann equation, then compare on-shell wall and Einstein actions. The normalization connection to Eq. (7.4) remains unresolved.
Find a direction whose derivative is at least the potential. Normalize it with the scalar metric, then apply Cauchy–Schwarz to obtain a uniform slope bound.

Use the Novikov–Thorne framework and conservation of mass, energy and angular momentum to obtain disk flux from circular-geodesic quantities. Determine the marginally stable orbit through the effective potential and its first two radial derivatives; the authors also report checking vertical stability.

Convert flux to temperature through the Stefan–Boltzmann law, assume local Planck emission, and integrate over the disk surface with inclination and gravitational-redshift factors. Metric dependence enters through orbital quantities, the inner disk radius and metric coefficients.

For every fixed common r2, choose each source's accretion rate, inclination and spin to minimize its optical-luminosity mismatch. Scan r2 and evaluate χ², Nash–Sutcliffe efficiency, index of agreement and their modified forms on these optimized predictions.
Apply the TCC inequality aF/aI<MPl/HF to Stage 3 and combine it with the weak-coupling duration bound and the expansion required by the horizon problem.

For a preliminary perturbation calculation, expand the Einstein-frame scalar sector to quadratic order in longitudinal gauge. Follow Fourier modes of the canonical variable v, taking oscillatory sub-Hubble evolution, growing super-Hubble behavior v∝a and crossing condition k=aHE.

Use the Stage 3 Einstein-frame solution HE=HI/[1−HI(tE−tI)] and aE=aI/[1−HI(tE−tI)]. Compare today's comoving Hubble scale with the initial Stage 3 Hubble patch, using H∝a and temperature scaling to translate sufficient expansion into a dilaton bound.

Split the dispersive integral at a high matching scale M*. Evaluate its Regge tail at fixed negative t, cancel its 1/t divergence against graviton exchange, and retain finite terms involving the residue function f and trajectory derivatives j′ and j″.

Reduce operators using integration by parts, Bianchi identities, the four-dimensional Gauss–Bonnet identity and perturbative field redefinitions. Compute amplitudes in a simplified Einstein-frame basis, including scalar loops using dimensional regularization and the paper's MS scheme.

Use Cauchy contour deformation, crossing symmetry and subtracted dispersion relations. Subtract scalar and graviton poles to define B, and subtract calculable low-energy absorptive contributions to obtain improved quantities BΛEFT.

Compute finite scalar mass corrections and estimate radiatively generated portal couplings using one-loop beta functions, βλ=dλ/d ln μ², with tree-level portals taken small. Inserting the induced Higgs–leptoquark quartic into a one-loop mass correction estimates an anomaly-dependent two-loop contribution; a separate electroweak two-loop correction is included.

Integrate out S3 and match to the weak effective theory; confront the resulting parameters with imported B-decay fits, neutral-meson mixing constraints and scalar-leptoquark pair-production searches. Phenomenology is evaluated in the gauge-sector decoupling limit.

Use the on-shell Euclidean action, Gibbons–Hawking term and holographic counterterms to obtain free energies; add a Maxwell boundary term for the fixed-charge ensemble. Apply the Iyer–Wald Hamiltonian variation to derive the boson-star first law.

Fit the chemical potential with a four-positive-parameter algebraic ansatz inspired by extremal RN-AdS, then integrate the first law to estimate M(Q). A generalized Smarr construction relates bulk integrals to surface terms; in the planar scaling regime, 3M=2μQ together with dM=μdQ gives μ∝Q1/2.

Numerically shoot outward from a tenth-order regular-origin Taylor expansion, starting slightly away from r=0 to avoid apparent 0/0 terms. Tune central data to the source-free boundary condition, extract asymptotic parameters by fitting and restore asymptotic time normalization.

The fluctuation enhancement G(Q) is fitted from numerical coupled inflaton–radiation perturbations, using the zero-shear gauge χ=0. The analytical spectral tilt uses a simplified strong-dissipation spectrum; numerical predictions use the fuller fitted expression.

The authors numerically evolve the full background system for n=2–5, tune Q* and α, and determine V0 using the adopted scalar-spectrum normalization. Analytical evolution equations for Q and the potential slow-roll parameters guide the field ranges.

Combine the flux-induced conifold F-term potential with the polarized NS5 probe potential, whose Z-dependence enters through warping. Locate simultaneous extrema and impose positivity of the radicand determining the conifold minimum.

Estimate invariant distance along a coupled (Z,ψ) trajectory using the Kähler metric and the NS5 small-velocity kinetic term. Bound the distance by the sum of separate Z and ψ contributions, then conservatively bound the ψ integral using the largest Z in its domain.

Minimize the effective potential in two treatments: keep τ1 fixed and vary the remaining moduli, or perform the authors' alternative minimization over all three moduli. Analytic extremum and positivity conditions are supplemented by parameterized potential plots.

Solve Dρ1W=0 at leading large volume using the Lambert W branches, then insert the critical τ1 into an expansion of the F-term potential. Separate purely perturbative, purely nonperturbative and mixed contributions.

Compute thermal matter stress tensors and Weyl-anomaly contributions, solve for the dilaton, and compare connected/disconnected partition functions. Cosmological candidates use complex-time contours; extremizing their matter partition function also determines, when possible, the temperature parameter.

Apply the imported quantum-extremal-surface/island prescription through replica twist operators. Extremize generalized entropy including endpoint dilatons; for long intervals, use a twist-operator OPE to approximate the two endpoint problems independently.

Fit finite-N numerical central charges and R-charges to large-N trends. Test the AdS WGC using charge-to-dimension ratios; with multiple U(1)s, construct normalized convex polygons or polyhedra and compare their boundary distances with the unit sphere.

Use gauge-anomaly cancellation and the one-loop asymptotic-freedom bound to enumerate matter contents. Determine candidate IR R-charges by a-maximization, and obtain chiral dimensions and central charges from R-symmetry anomalies.

Iterate a-maximization while removing unitarity-violating operators, implemented through flip fields X_O and W=X_O O. Hilbert-series techniques are used to examine gauge-invariant operator content and relations.
Integrate the kinetic identity along H(a), then eliminate a from U(a). The output preserves the input equation-of-state dependence and matches background total stress-energy.

Convert the entropy constraint to a potential envelope using Friedmann evolution, then differentiate with a stated saturation or slack condition. The paper applies this operation to interpret vacuumon slopes during the proposed exit.

A proposed sequence of effective descriptions connected by state decoupling, gravitational-wave condensation, and matter-producing phase transitions. It separates stiff inflationary matter, subsequent radiation, and a later massive axion.

Derives local island constraints using mutual-information monotonicity, strong subadditivity, and a narrow collar regulating entropy. Rewrites extremality as ∂λ Sgen(I)=∂λ Imat(I,R), allowing bounds independent of a particular auxiliary R.

Obtains FRW matter entropy by Weyl transforming thermofield-double entropy. Relative-entropy arguments bound deformation derivatives by |∂η f|, |∂r f|≤1; explicit holographic entropy functions permit a more detailed island calculation.
Uses the imported island prescription S(R)=min ext_I Sgen(I∪R), with Sgen=Area(∂I)/4+Smat(I∪R)−Sct(∂I). Nonempty extrema must beat the always-available empty island.

Measures the boundary gravitational Hamiltonian, expressed through the subleading metric falloff in Fefferman–Graham gauge. Repeated energy measurements determine the probability of the unique zero-energy outcome, mathematically ⟨P0⟩ with P0=|0⟩⟨0|.

After removing vacuum overlap by a known preliminary unitary when necessary, probes quadratic response to small sources. Sums with real and imaginary reference operators determine complex overlaps; energy-eigenspace probabilities resolve the remaining correlated phase ambiguity.

Uses vacuum cyclicity and analyticity to obtain a dense set of states from short-time-band operators. An explicit construction approximates single-particle states by compact-time smearing and extends to multiparticle states through the weakly coupled Fock-space description.
Euclidean BCFT path integrals prepare pure states and calculate their observables. The gravity description uses a dominant classical saddle and analytic continuation of its ETW-brane geometry.

Auxiliary operators are replaced formally by source variables using delta functionals, and their path integral generates a joint source distribution. The paper also reviews large-N scaling and all-orders perturbative analyses of gauge-singlet multi-trace couplings.

The authors solve gauge-fixed Einstein-DeTurck elliptic equations using Newton-Raphson iteration on a nonuniform finite-element grid. They report using a 200×300 grid and requiring relative error below 10⁻⁵, with refinement near large-gradient regions approaching singular solutions.

They first find scalar zero modes on fixed Einstein-Maxwell backgrounds, then construct backreacted stationary hairy solutions. Diagnostics include the boundary condensate ⟨O2⟩ and the spacetime maximum of the Kretschmann scalar K; growth of maximum K under decreasing q identifies the numerical approach to a singular branch.

Supersymmetric localization gives a Coulomb-branch integral with a magnetic-flux sum. Phase-dependent convergent contours and residue calculations select contributing poles; Gamma reflection identities reorganize the result into sector contributions involving I-functions and Gamma-class quotients.

The authors expand I-functions and characteristic classes in base cohomology, evaluate intersection or residue pairings, and compare the resulting expressions with FJRW theory and mirror symmetry. For the two-parameter hybrid proposal they report a Picard-Fuchs annihilation check on the six period components.

The authors match the shell’s extrinsic-curvature discontinuity to its dust stress tensor, with m=4πR²σ. Solving the junction equation gives M′=M+(q²−m²−2qQ)/(2R)−m√(fII(R)+v²), where fII=1−2M/R+Q²/R². This is the paper’s classical shell calculation.

They take R→∞ to obtain M′=M−m√(1+v∞²), combine this with charge conservation and the imposed nonincrease of Q/M, and separately examine the outward velocity needed for escape from the original horizon.

Replace detailed potential evolution by initial value, slope, and curvature under thawing assumptions. Evaluate the analytic trajectory and velocity at the approximate ΛCDM age. Applicability requires checking local-potential and background approximations for the potential being modeled.

Transform an existing allowed region through deterministic model relations and overlay a theoretical threshold. Here, present equation-of-state constraints become initial-slope and field-excursion constraints. The operation does not provide a new fit or remove the input region's prior dependence.
Differentiate the complete polynomial F, retain H' = H_0 beta, substitute into the full background and tilt expressions, impose energy and branch inequalities, and test the alpha = 0 limit.

Prescribe F(H) and H(phi), enforce canonical energy conservation, solve the field velocity, and integrate the expansion. This is an imported background reconstruction operation rather than a model-independent prescription for gravitational perturbations.

Use the tree-level impact-parameter phase shift δ=(1/2s)∫d²q/(2π)² exp(iq·b)Mtree. Apply the causal signal-transmission requirement that δ grow no faster than s and be nonnegative when growing with s; coherent states and independent shockwaves provide a time-delay interpretation.

Apply the imported CKSZ asymptotic uniqueness argument after establishing gravitational higher-spin exchanges. The string-amplitude appendix reviews a worldsheet saddle-point evaluation of the leading high-energy four-point amplitude.

Start from the imported unique causal four-dimensional G_JG_Jh vertex, normalized by the soft theorem. For distinct particles, combine soft-graviton suppression with phase-shift matrix positivity, |δ_GG′|²≤δ_GGδ_G′G′, to suppress identity-changing vertices by inverse powers of Λgr. Interference between G_J and graviton superpositions then constrains the s^(J−1) exchange contribution.

Numerical multifield FRW evolution is compared with slow-roll analytic approximations. Linear Fourier-mode perturbations and their mixed mass matrix are used to assess whether hadronic fluctuations affect axion fluctuations at horizon exit.

The paper reviews probing faithful global symmetries with fractional color, flavor and baryon fluxes on a large Euclidean four-torus, then following the anomalous partition-function phase into the IR using anomaly matching.

A two-light-quark chiral Lagrangian, with equal quark masses for simplicity, illustrates the axion-pion product-cosine potential. This illustration is distinguished from the heavy-fermion UV construction, where chiral perturbation theory is unavailable.

The domain-wall/cosmology dictionary uses analytic continuation q̄=−iq and N̄=−iN. Stress-tensor correlator coefficients determine cosmological power spectra; global currents source bulk gauge perturbations. S-duality inversion is then invoked for magnetic-current correlators.

Planar one- and two-loop current correlators are evaluated in momentum space using dimensional regularization, including gauge-field insertions in the currents. Direct integration and reduction to a supplied integral basis are used; the author reports agreement for the relevant divergences.

Estimate graviton-mediated production using A_i∼E²/Mpl² and Σ_iσ_i∼NE²/Mpl⁴. For monojet plus missing energy, approximate the additional phase-space suppression by dividing the 2→2 estimate by (4π)³, then compare with uncertainties quoted for LHC invisible processes.

Use Hawking lifetime scaling and order-of-magnitude spin-extraction formulas. For degenerate scalars Γ∼N_B a r_g⁸m⁹; the adapted fermionic estimate is Γ∼N_F a r_g⁵m⁶. Compare these rates with black-hole timescales and the angular-momentum occupation requirement.

Generalize phase-space counting: one power of the species requirement comes from the increasing particle number needed at lower mass, and three powers come from phase space. The resulting density bound is combined with upper limits on the inclusive number of species.

Use the Lorentzian smeared density ρ(r)=μ√β/[π²(r²+β)²]. The paper first obtains a shape function through the F=1 relation ρ=b′/r², fixes its integration constant at the throat, and uses the curvature relation R=2b′/r².

Attempt an f(R) reconstruction from F=df/dR=r²ρ/b′, substituting the stated r(R)=√(2b′/R), expressing F(R), and integrating to the displayed f(R). Test material combinations ρ+p_r and ρ+p_t using the modified field equations, followed by an effective radial NEC test.
Use Euclidean bounce rates Γ=P exp(−S). In the flat-space thin-wall limit, S scales as T⁴/(ΔΛ)³ and P as T⁴/(ΔΛ)²; numerical factors are generally omitted.

Count nucleations in a causally accessible spacetime region, truncate at an initial hypersurface, and differentiate the volume in observer proper time. The application neglects backreaction and contains no displayed collision-survival correction.

Approximate the ridge by a concave quadratic, solve for field positions at specified energy levels, and compare the initial-to-top distance with the full width. The image-confirmed square root makes the source's simplification internally consistent.

Coarse-grain discrete transitions into energy change per unit time, then match that quantity to an assumed slow-roll description. This operation estimates a scalar slope under normalization and dynamical assumptions.

Integrate nucleation over an observer’s past light cone with collision-survival probabilities to obtain dN/dt=ΓVeff. Matching the magnitude of averaged energy discharge to slow roll gives (|V′|/V)²∼ΔΛ ΓVeff/Λ^(3/2) when up-tunneling is neglected. With Γ denoting the down-tunneling rate, the paper’s net-discharge prescription (B.18) multiplies this squared-slope relation by f=1−exp(−ΔΛ/Λ²). Retain f near β=2 when assessing coefficients. Identifying V with Λ here is only at scaling accuracy, subject to the stated normalization caveat.

Turn an evaluated counting integral into a self-consistency equation, eliminate a common coordinate factor, and solve for the physical stationary rate. The supplied pages expose the algebra but omit the preceding integral construction.

Inspect representations in previously computed elliptic genera, compare circle-reduced GSWS and Chern–Simons couplings, and use torsional-section homology relations to constrain representations of wrapped M2-brane states.

Activate C2=w2(G/Z(G)) in H²(M6,Z(G)); use the fractional instanton density I4=αG P(C2) mod Z and its GSWS coupling to compute shifts under large tensor gauge transformations. Local counterterms are examined for whether both tensor and center transformations remain consistent.

Include string surface operators and the modified Bianchi identity dHᶦ=I4ᶦ+Qᶦσ4. Tadpole cancellation requires [I4ᶦ]=−Qᶦσ4; pairing induced charges with the string lattice then tests Dirac quantization.

Solve the momentum-space position eigenproblem using x̂=iħz(p)∂p and a momentum-space weight involving 1/z(p). An arctangent phase supplies a modified wavelength; a COW neutron-interference analogy then motivates a momentum-dependent gravitational field strength.

Use a Riemann-tensor tidal component and geodesic deviation for virtual-particle separation, followed by position–momentum and energy–time uncertainty inequalities, to estimate a characteristic momentum for insertion into the effective Newton constant.

Introduce Painlevé-type coordinates and radial null trajectories for the action approach. Because the radial action remains difficult to evaluate, use Newman–Penrose spin coefficients, combined spin-field equations, a WKB mode ansatz and graphical energy solutions.

For products of SU(n_i), test cyclic subgroups using sum_i k_i^2 m_i(n_i−1)/(2n_i) in Z, with k_i l = 0 modulo n_i. The authors describe an exhaustive integer scan subject to rank(G) <= 18 and reduction of other groups' contributions to SU-subgroup contributions.

Couple center symmetry to two-form backgrounds. Fractional instanton number, expressed through the Pontryagin square P, gives the partition-function phase exp(2πi A), with A = sum_i m_i alpha_Gi integral[b4 cup P(C2^(i))], under a large B4 gauge transformation.
Compare the anomaly condition with Mordell–Weil torsion and the discriminant quadratic form of the lattice generated by non-affine components of reducible K3 fibers.

Five regional best-fit models seed a VPFIT reoptimization with separate α parameters for individual components or small groups. Weak or blended components are grouped to give 47 estimates. Least trimmed squares removes 15% in each region, leaving 40 estimates.

LFC calibration uses eight seventh-order polynomials per echelle order and a single high-flux reference exposure; ThAr calibration uses one third-order polynomial per order and the immediately preceding calibration frame. Exposures receive individual barycentric corrections before weighted co-addition.

AI-VPFIT builds Voigt-profile models through a genetic procedure with trial components and AICc complexity selection. Shared component redshifts and broadening parameters are linked across species, column densities are free, and continuum, saturated-line zero levels and unidentified interlopers are accommodated.

WKB and Euclidean path-integral saddle methods describe tunnelling. Integration over the instanton time produces a time prefactor; bounce fluctuations and a negative mode connect the saddle to decay, with Γ ∼ exp(−Sbounce) only at exponential accuracy.

Wilsonian operator expansion and heavy-field elimination supplemented by loop thresholds. Full running and matching is described, but the illustrative toy models deliberately use classical elimination plus loop corrections as a shortcut.

Superspace D/F-term actions and algebraic elimination of auxiliary fields organize SUSY models. Holomorphy and spurion charge constraints underpin the presented perturbative Wilsonian superpotential non-renormalisation argument.

Use Pin bordism to motivate defects and compactify on inversion quotients. For 9d, project the massless spectrum on T³/Z₂ and impose the 6d gravitational condition 273 = 29nT + nH − nV. For 8d, compute the reduced 5d parity anomaly using η invariants and Ω₆^Pin− = Z₁₆.

Generalize Dirac quantization to an RP² angular geometry, including the electric probe's worldvolume anomaly. A Majorana Pin− fermion contributes η(RP²) = 1/8; eight BPS or sixteen non-BPS goldstino modes give no net phase. The authors use supersymmetry to exclude additional anomalous internal sectors and infer integer I₅ magnetic charge.

Define an entropic parameter S_Amax(ω‖ω∘E), comparing the vacuum with its lift through a conditional expectation onto the additive algebra. E preserves additive observables and removes nontrivial nonlocal sectors. Relative entropy also applies to type-III QFT algebras.

Restricting relative entropy to chosen nonlocal operator algebras gives lower bounds; certainty and complementary restrictions give upper bounds. Character projectors reduce the finite Abelian subalgebra calculation to log|G|−H(p), not generally the full regional entropy.

Solve abelian D-flatness by first overshooting in negative charge directions and then correcting each component independently. The operation applies to the specified fixed charge spectrum and unbounded formal field space; it does not establish EFT validity, F-flatness or stable bound-state existence.

Suppress interactions through large string-unit triangle areas between intersections, then evaluate which products of condensates enter superpotential derivatives. Small coefficients alone do not ensure small F-terms uniformly as charges or expectation values grow.

Bound flux through charge cancellation, then translate the bounded flux data into a finite set of supersymmetric moduli solutions. The source supplies the logical outline rather than the flux lattice, explicit equations or enumeration.

Use charged open-string condensation to cancel effective FI contributions and interpret the condensates as recombination. Apply this operation near mutually supersymmetric branes; separately test F-flatness, moduli stabilization and whether the retained fields remain light.

Evolve admissible disturbances and test whether the effective description remains controlled. Barrier-crossing scalar disturbances provide the paper's application; approach to high curvature indicates failure of its present calculational framework.

Solve the spacelike boundary-value problem approaching the false vacuum, then continue and match into the timelike region. This constructs a specific classical solution rather than demonstrating that general initial data evolve toward it.

Select terms, solve stationarity, and audit claimed small parameters along a specified flux family. Large radius, weak coupling, omitted-term dominance, and suppression of higher-order operators must each be checked.

Insert a slowly moving large-radius kink, integrate across its wall, and add the interior energy difference. Audit the action and energy before using the radius potential; the source requires unresolved kinetic, lambda, and epsilon conventions.

Formal interactions use an A∞ construction from higher-spin algebra. AdS5 deformations are realized through universal enveloping algebra/Joseph relations and through quasi-conformal realization using canonical oscillator pairs.

Vacuum one-loop determinants use spectral zeta functions of transverse-traceless kinetic operators, subtract gauge ghosts, and include fermionic statistics signs. Infinite spin sums require regularization; an exponential cutoff with finite-part extraction is used.
Chiral amplitudes are calculated using Feynman diagrams and Berends–Giele off-shell currents; unitarity cuts are used for the complete one-loop n-point amplitude.

Insert the metric into the mass spectrum and gas action, identify the nonderivative term, and vary with respect to retained moduli. This paper applies an imported operation to a toroidal shape variable.

Suppress thermally excited states, retain the lowest-mass sector, and insert its moduli-dependent mass into the gas action. The procedure requires an appropriate thermal hierarchy and a consistent identification of the retained charge branch.

Apply a locally constant-coefficient oscillatory ansatz to the reduced scalar equations and solve the determinant. A low-wavenumber Taylor expansion and dominance of its leading term require separate checks when that term has a small coefficient.

Integrate the polar scalar equations with matter and radiation, vary the radial mass, and adjust the vacuum-energy offset for the chosen present cosmology. Track the full potential-gradient norm and scalar equation of state to diagnose spinning dark energy.

Project the background equations onto a moving orthonormal frame. The tangent equation measures evolution of speed against friction; the normal equation measures turning. Alternatively, obtain Ω directly by contracting the antisymmetric velocity-gradient tensor on an on-shell trajectory.

Solve the radial linear perturbation equations for four rotating metric functions. The general solution has six integration constants; asymptotic flatness, a static normalized frame, fixed mass and angular momentum, and a chosen horizon regularity condition select the branch studied.

Use Wald entropy and near-horizon expansions, with an order-one non-extremality parameter replacing the singular fixed-parameter expansion near extremality. In the charged theory, perturbative field redefinitions organize nine four-derivative structures into four inequivalent classes.

Derive general background and slow-roll equations, construct the supergravity scalar potential and leading large-volume field metric, then numerically evolve the inflaton, spectator scalars and isotropic gauge amplitude.

Expand perturbations to quadratic order. Tensor modes receive both slow-roll analytic treatment and numerical evolution without that approximation; scalar analysis uses ADM lapse/shift constraints and numerical evolution.

Approximate amplified gauge tensors by Whittaker functions with constant ξQ, ξh and ξf, source metric tensors with a Green function, and estimate backreaction using mode integrals cut off around the transiently amplified region.

Integrate the spectral-index or tensor-ratio equation for V(N), prescribe an independent slope ε(N), solve algebraically for L(N), and integrate and invert φ(N). Positivity, monotonicity, interval restrictions, and perturbation conventions must be checked before applying the output.

Canonically reparametrize the single scalar and transform slopes and distances by the chain rule. Applied conditionally to the conjectures, this exposes the field-normalization assumption behind the paper's claimed reconciliation.

Branch supermultiplets and symmetry representations, then retain invariant subsectors. The quaternionic-to-complex truncation retains a U(1)-invariant sector; a further Z₂-invariant restriction yields the real magical theory.

Compare gauge potentials whose non-metric graviton field strength contains one or two derivatives. The field strength is an exchange-symmetric (3,3) tensor, self-dual in each triple; the two potential formulations describe the same underlying unitary physical multiplet.

Extend the internal coordinates by a singlet Y• and use the section constraint C^{IJK}∂J⊗∂K − (1/√10)Δ^{IJ}(∂J⊗∂• + ∂•⊗∂J) = 0. Δ is a constant background tensor. Taking ∂I = 0 selects the non-metric section; Jordan C-tensors organize the proposed unified extensions.
Diagonalise anomaly-induced axion mass matrices perturbatively in the QCD contribution relative to hidden confinement, then obtain photon interactions from anomaly couplings and axion–meson mixing.
Use two-light-quark chiral perturbation theory to match axion–meson interactions, identify physical CP phases, and minimise the anomaly-induced effective potential.

The proposed moose-like diagrams encode axions, fermion U(1) charges, gauge representations and fermion masses. Cancellation equations are read by summing gauge-to-axion paths, including anomaly multiplicities and composite-current normalisations.

Analyse a probe string with the Nambu–Goto action in the perturbative background of a stationary heavy string, using worldsheet gauges t=τ and σ=z. Compare radial motion with the endpoint geodesic and compare energies of radial and tilted configurations.

Interpret subtraction through an exterior-boundary curvature counterterm and holographic renormalisation. Review an earlier transverse-traceless propagator construction using scalar Green functions, Bessel modes and junction conditions.

Use thin-shell junction conditions to obtain cosmological expansion and effective gravitational scales. Separately integrate the warped five-dimensional Einstein–Hilbert term with a radial cutoff to expose divergent and finite contributions.

Numerically solve V=Vz=0 for Minkowski vacuum trajectories, then allow a small positive vacuum energy. Canonical normalization uses dφ/dz=√(2G(z)), followed by numerical inversion. The gauge coupling sets the overall potential scale after the stated μ/g parametrizations.

Combine near-origin potential slow-roll estimates with homogeneous FLRW evolution and Hubble slow-roll parameters. Evaluate observables at the beginning of the last 60 e-folds and fix g using the scalar amplitude. The paper's historical Planck benchmark is ns=0.9649±0.0042 and As≈1.96×10⁻⁹.

Analytically continue the large-complex-structure prepotential toward a shrinking-curve conifold. Resum the unsuppressed worldsheet multiple-cover contributions using polylogarithm reflection identities, while retaining a controlled expansion in the conifold modulus and instantons on the remaining large curves.

Construct the geometry using toric and Greene–Plesser methods, and enumerate restricted fluxes by quadratic Diophantine equations in a finite integer search. The D3 tadpole is calculated both from the resolved orientifold via Lefschetz and directly in the orbifold limit; the authors report agreement.

Three-step stabilization: choose integer fluxes making the polynomial superpotential vanish along zi=piτ; integrate out orthogonal moduli; stabilize the conifold modulus through its logarithmic period and stabilize the remaining flat direction by a bulk-instanton racetrack. The Wilsonian ordering depends on the resulting mass hierarchy.

Use three stabilization steps: solve the polynomial Uα sector at Z=0 with vanishing superpotential; stabilize Z exponentially in S; then balance instanton and conifold contributions in an effective racetrack superpotential for S. Approximate minima provide starting points for numerical searches in the full eight-real-field potential.

Solve Picard–Fuchs equations using local power-log series. Monodromy and a moduli-independent bilinear symplectic form constrain the transformation to integral symplectic periods; numerical matching in overlapping convergence regions fixes remaining freedoms.

Analytically continue a hypergeometric period basis toward the conifold, evaluate parameter derivatives through harmonic polylogarithms, and match to the local Picard–Fuchs basis. The resulting transition matrix permits computation of the mirror map and prepotential.

Introduce U and Z, vary the multiplier to obtain the constrained representation, and retain boundary terms when eliminating fields. With field strength fixed at the boundary, integrate the three-form equation to a flux constant and evaluate its contribution with the boundary term included.

Compute or import the Euclidean action difference for membrane nucleation, insert the physical tension and released vacuum energy, and estimate the rate through e^(−B). The calculation used here omits the prefactor and expands about a nearly Minkowski exterior.

Apply the first-order three-form dualization to the strongly warped KKLT action, shift to ordinary nilpotency, then remove the common superpotential phase by an imaginary modulus shift and chiral-density transformation.

Linearize ExFT equations and replace internal differentiation by dressed harmonic-action matrices T_A. Mass matrices depend on X and T; scalar contributions organize as XX+XT+TT. Diagonalized modes can be mapped back through the ExFT/supergravity dictionary.

Use generalized Scherk-Schwarz reduction and a global generalized frame satisfying L_UM UN=X_MN^P UP. Dressing the frame with the vacuum scalar vielbein produces the corresponding dressed embedding tensor.

Expand every fluctuation using the same complete basis of scalar harmonics; the generalized vielbein carries its tensor structure. Choose harmonics at the maximally symmetric scalar configuration, which need not itself solve the equations of motion.

Construct an invariant, Yang-Mills-like Lagrangian before subdivision, without a conventional spacetime kinetic term. Vary generator amplitudes and a pure-state density matrix to obtain equilibrium equations.

Define relational time by comparing changes in clock and system states relative to an observer. One example uses the absolute change of a clock expectation value as dt and defines the system Hamiltonian through dρ_s/dt=−i[H_s,ρ_s]/ℏ.
Invoke the rescaled N→∞ limit of SU(N) generators, their differential representation through spherical harmonics and Poisson brackets, and a claimed Cartan/Pauli-matrix decomposition.

Analyze alternative stabilization schemes using F-term and D-term constraints, then combine tadpole/Hodge-number identities with imported empirical scaling laws for controlled cycle volumes at large h1,1.

Treat the warp-factor equation as compact-space electrostatics, -∇̃²h = gs ρ̃D3. Compare its generic variation from localized throat charge with the cycle-averaged warp factor fixed by uplift matching; use local Taylor estimates, a Hessian argument near extrema, and coarse graining of O3 sources.

An explicitly integrated S6 electrostatic toy model illustrates both a large negative warp-factor region and screening by a specially arranged shell of negative charge. It is illustrative rather than a Calabi–Yau compactification: S6 has no nontrivial four-cycle supporting the modeled E3.

Evaluate the on-shell Euclidean action including the Gibbons–Hawking–York boundary term, which supplies a throat-boundary contribution. Translate action suppression into local symmetry-violating EFT operators and estimate axion potentials, masses, and mixing.

Numerically solve the coupled scalar and Einstein ordinary differential equations using shooting, favoring the second-order equation for R for numerical stability. Fit the resulting actions as functions of symmetry-breaking scales, charges, scalar couplings, and asymptotic string coupling.

Derive equations in fixed-charge sectors using either dependent angular/radial variables or a Lagrange multiplier enforcing charge conservation. The authors emphasize the resulting angular-term sign change relative to naive unconstrained variation.

Bayesian MCMC inference compares hierarchical timing/noise models containing zero, one, or two common-spectrum processes with uncorrelated, HD, monopolar, or dipolar structures. Product-space sampling estimates model odds.

The optimal statistic estimates pairwise correlated power using fixed noise and noise marginalization over 10,000 posterior noise vectors. Additional Bayesian tests separate auto- and cross-correlation amplitudes and reconstruct the angular correlation function with a seven-node spline.

Dropout analyses and factorized-likelihood calculations assess individual pulsar support. Random Fourier phase shifts and sky scrambles generate null distributions for HD statistics while retaining a common-spectrum red process.

Use the imported thin-wall Coleman–de Luccia estimate τ≈exp{(24π²/|Vshallow|)(C−1)^4/[C²(2C−1)²]}, with C²=|Vdeep|/|Vshallow| before uplift. Evaluate minima numerically to assess attainable lifetimes and parameter tuning.

Analyze the supergravity F-term potential using DρW=0 for supersymmetric extrema and additionally W=0 for Minkowski. Grouping equal exponential rates shows that at least three distinct groups are needed for a nontrivial stabilized supersymmetric Minkowski solution at W0=0; perturb A1 to obtain a shallow AdS minimum.

Expand curvature, G-flux and quantum operators in powers of gs and Mp; study the X8 curvature polynomial and integrated flux equations. Include perturbative terms, nonlocal instanton contributions and a stress-tensor consistency condition for fermionic condensates.

Inputs the actual nonthermal distribution into CLASS to compute background and linear perturbations, CMB temperature spectra and linear matter power spectra. Analytic estimates of ΔNeff, free-streaming scale and sterile density guide benchmark selection; CLASS uses the full distribution.

Numerically evolves decaying matter and sourced radiation, with transfer terms −ρmat/τ and +ρmat/τ and a Friedmann background. Radiation includes both the Standard Model and daughters, which are highly relativistic during production.

Adapts previously obtained decay-energy spectra: parent abundance decreases exponentially, each daughter starts with energy mφ/2, and the daughter energy redshifts with the scale factor. Isotropy and subsequent free streaming convert this spectrum into today's momentum distribution.

For periodic scalar potentials U = fa²μ0²[1 − cos(φ/fa)], models self-interaction interruption through a bosenova occupation threshold NBose. Uses the modified criterion ΓSR τBH(NBose/NMax) > ln NBose to estimate exclusions in the mass–decay-constant plane.

Constructs mass–spin Regge exclusion contours using ΓSR τBH ≥ ln NMax. A sufficiently spinning observed black hole crossing a contour excludes the corresponding boson mass under the assumed evolutionary history. Reports individual and ensemble confidence bounds using adopted prior methodology.

Imports linear instability rates: scalar Klein–Gordon separation and matched asymptotics; nonrelativistic matched-asymptotic Proca solutions; and tensor rates inferred using long-wavelength black-hole absorption probabilities. These analytical ingredients are reviewed rather than newly derived.

Imports a dilaton anomaly effective action, applies a trace-anomaly dilation identity and an approximate factorization to estimate the scalar two-point function, then Fourier transforms at equal times. Uses anomaly interaction scaling and the in-in formalism for higher-point predictions.

Reviews the BV construction from a Weyl topological action and analyzes BRST transformations, ghost numbers and candidate local terms. Uses this field-content analysis to argue that the Einstein–Hilbert term is forbidden.

Expose P(2,3,1) fibrations through SL(6,Z) transformations and fine, regular, star triangulations. Identify E8 rays by ord(f,g)=(4,5), then blow up colliding E8 divisors and residual non-toric non-minimal loci.

Compute gravitational anomalies by summing moduli, gravity, 3–7 and 7–7 sectors using characteristic classes and π*c4. The authors test generalized Hirzebruch examples with non-Higgsable groups; for singular toric bases they instead use combinatorial signature and arithmetic-genus data.

Use Batyrev dual reflexive polytopes and toric anticanonical hypersurfaces; compute stringy Hodge numbers through lattice-point and face-interior counts. Landau-Ginzburg methods supply additional Hodge numbers for the extremal example.

Field-theory methods include Wilsonian momentum-shell integration, dimensional regularization with minimal subtraction, RG evolution and threshold matching. The noncommutative formulation uses the Weyl-Wigner map; auxiliary fields formally encode infrared terms.

Thermal evolution is described through sector energy/entropy content and bulk heat flow while each sector remains internally thermalized. The dark-matter study calculates the freeze-in yield of twin electrons.

Collider forecasts reconstruct displaced secondary vertices from paired, hadronically decaying LLPs, using explicit clustering and isolation to estimate leading irreducible backgrounds and select analysis cuts.

Choose a special complex structure locus first, construct algebraic surfaces whose dual classes are of type (2,2), and ask whether their flux combinations trap the model there. Evaluate G_IJ=∫_X G4∧D_I D_J Ω; its rank is the paper's criterion for the number of stabilized complex structure directions.

Represent primitive middle cohomology by residues PΩ0/Q^{5-p}. At Fermat, quotient homogeneous polynomials by the Jacobi ideal ⟨x_i^5⟩. Degree-six monomials describe deformations, and second derivatives reduce G_IJ to periods of degree-twelve numerators over algebraic cycles.

Use imported algebraic-cycle period formulas and automorphism characters to evaluate the rank matrix. For linear cycles, symmetry determines relative period coefficients up to overall normalization; it does not determine all periods of a full algebraic-cycle basis from one orbit. General complete-intersection periods use a determinant identity modulo the Jacobi ideal.

Harish–Chandra characters encode global single-particle representations. Their regulated Fourier transforms define static-patch spectral densities; character integrals compute quasicanonical thermodynamics and sphere determinants. Tools include covariant Pauli–Villars/heat-kernel regularization, Hubbard–Stratonovich transformation, contour deformation, Hurwitz zeta functions and residue sums.

For massive symmetric spin s, locality motivates extending the TT eigenvalue sum from n≥s to n≥−1, admitting formal negative degeneracies. For massless fields, negative-mode contour rotations and zero-mode removal become character flipping: c_k q^k→−c_k q^(−k) for k<0, with k=0 terms dropped; residual gauge-volume division restores locality.

For algebraic attractors, applies the imported Shiga–Wolfart period criterion, then refines the Jacobian map to a Prym map into a PEL Shimura variety. Injectivity of its derivative fixes the image dimension. Special-subvariety codimensions and a claimed large-monodromy result supply the unlikely-intersection argument.

Establishes equivalence of algebraicity for X and its associated curve C using spreading out, automorphisms, the covering morphism recovered from a line bundle, normality/Hartogs arguments and reconstruction of the branch configuration.

Uses imported Hodge-structure results identifying the cyclic eigenspace H^(2n−3)(X)[i] with the (2n−3)rd exterior power of H¹(C)[i]. The curve eigenspaces have Hodge numbers (2i−1, 2(n−i)−1), allowing the attractor condition to be expressed through a one-dimensional space of holomorphic forms.

Uses leading perturbative entropy Sent=−λ²log(λ̃²)∑|C̃n,N|². Negligible squeezing and slowly varying coupling permit approximately time-independent matrix elements. Momentum integrals are evaluated using p3≪p2, and comoving entropy density is divided by a³ to obtain physical density.

Splits the scalar-mode Hilbert space into super-Hubble modes as system and sub-Hubble modes as bath, tracing their interaction-induced entanglement in Fourier space. Sub-Hubble physical momenta have a Planck cutoff; an infrared cutoff kI restricts the counted super-Hubble modes.

With constant ε and a constant dominant ζ mode, neglects nonlocal terms and selects the cubic interaction S3=MPl²∫dt d³x aε²ζ(∂ζ)². In canonical variables its effective coupling is λ=√ε/(2√2 aMPl), with dimensionless coupling λ̃=λΛ.
Resolve metric modes, choose a background-covariant gauge, and consistently include its scalar-background prefactor. The reported α=β=0 limit removes one scalar metric contribution.

Integrate ultraviolet-complete trajectories after checking their persistence near the fixed point, impose gravitational decoupling at M_Pl, and follow symmetry breaking until threshold freeze-out. The source performs the integrations; no numerical reproduction was undertaken.
Evaluate the flow at λ_HP=0. A nonzero additive source removes that point as a fixed point. On the reported FP3 branch, finite non-minimal couplings generated by Yukawas provide this source.

Balance the matter source for the curvature coupling against direct gravitational running, then compare the resulting root with the interval needed for positive f_y. Degenerate coefficients and omitted higher orders require separate treatment.

Use canonical dimensions to choose a finite operator basis, then test whether interacting exponents stay near their canonical values. This supports internal consistency but supplies no rigorous error estimate for omitted interactions.

Use near-canonical exponents and stability under restoring full anomalous-dimension dependence as complementary diagnostics. These test aspects of the chosen truncation but do not bound every omitted operator.

Linearize the RG flow, diagonalize its stability matrix, and distinguish IR-attractive constrained directions from IR-repulsive free directions. Mixing means that a prediction generally concerns a combination of couplings.

Construct mode-specific background-covariant regulators and track auxiliary scalar dependence with α_reg. This separates technical background choices from dynamical fields, whose additional appearance would alter the flow structure.

Expand the mass flow in the weak-gravity matter regime, discard the stated mass-dependent corrections and solve the remaining linear equation. The result applies to the fixed-point branch, not to arbitrary independently chosen matter couplings.
Use expectation values and quartics as broken-phase coordinates, expand about the minimum, and obtain scalar masses from the Hessian. The quartic normalization is specific to Eq. (43).

Differentiate B1 with respect to the scalar field and translate the result using εi definitions. The source supplies the operation, but omitted Eq. (15) prevents reconstruction of explicit parameter flows. The supplied image resolves the epsilon notation.

Evaluate the functional flow, project it onto a finite operator basis, search for simultaneous beta-function zeros, and analyze their stability. Nontrivial denominators retain mass thresholds and automatic decoupling.

Compute and solve the anomalous-dimension equation, evaluate it at a reference fixed point, scan individual couplings, and compare feedback-corrected fixed-point data. Interpret small shifts as a restricted robustness diagnostic rather than an error estimate.

Use a finite interval of near-fixed-point RG evolution to erase some initial-condition dependence, then evolve through gravitational decoupling. The resulting predictions are approximate and depend on attraction, duration, and crossover behavior.

Duplicate the single-sector equations, add the cross-sector terms, and exchange labels for the reciprocal contributions. Keep sector parameters independent and retain the threshold restrictions of each supplied equation.
Derive the determinant before dropping any background factors. Compare the consistent ghost action with the deliberately omitted-prefactor treatment to diagnose artificial dependence on α_GF.

Differentiate and rescale the potential flow, then study local slope and curvature together. Restore dimensionful derivatives and use the appropriate physical frame before comparing with cosmological observables.

Sweep auxiliary background parameters, track exponent shifts and look for changes of sign or stationary sensitivity. Compare these residual dependencies with the expected technical-choice independence of exact physical exponents.
Project graviton-scalar diagrams containing non-minimal vertices onto the Yukawa interaction and combine them with the imported minimal gravitational term and universal matter contribution.
Evaluate the regulated fermion trace using momentum integration or Dirac-spectrum summation, project onto potential and curvature operators, and add the result to the scalar-gravity flow.
Differentiate β_ξ at ξ=0 and reverse its sign to obtain the diagonal critical exponent. A full stability analysis must include off-diagonal derivatives involving the scalar mass and quartic coupling.

The reported workflow compares free-spectrum bin posteriors and power-law amplitude–slope contours with theoretical spectra. Named timing and sampling packages produced the contour plot, but the packet does not supply a reproducible statistical configuration.

Use a simulation-calibrated source template with A approximately 3 and B approximately 1, then determine its normalization and peak from the transition parameters. The operation supplies initial spectral energy rather than a complete bubble-collision simulation.

Normalize a subhorizon population by energy, propagate its modes through de Sitter expansion, and evaluate the superhorizon limit. The source spectrum remains an input rather than being derived by this transfer operation.

Estimate the wall tension, evaluate the thin-wall bounce action, and retain the leading tunneling exponential. The application supplies an approximate time-dependent rate without its prefactor or a resolved bounce solution.

Propagate the primordial spectrum to the present, convert k to cyclic frequency, and translate the resulting energy density into PTA strain variables. A pivot amplitude is distinct from a statistical fit over multiple bins.
Normalize the emitted tensor population using its energy density, evolve the rescaled modes, and evaluate the late superhorizon power with the same polarization convention.

Five running couplings are considered. Within the approximation, matter interactions do not backreact on the gravitational beta functions, so G* and Λ* are determined first and then inserted into the matter fixed-point equations.

Functional renormalization group using the Wetterich equation and a finite effective-action truncation. Fixed-point searches track collisions and departures into the complex plane as gauge strength or fermion number changes.

The reviewed diagnostic uses Fierz rearrangement and a Hubbard–Stratonovich auxiliary scalar: a divergent four-fermion interaction indicates the onset of a negative auxiliary mass squared and possible spontaneous symmetry breaking.

Linearize field equations, separate tensor/vector/scalar sectors, impose gauge constraints, and expand in internal harmonics. Static interval fluctuations become Schrödinger problems; AdS masses are compared with spin-dependent BF bounds.

For the proposed holographic interpretation, adopt the Ryu–Takayanagi prescription and compute regularized geodesic lengths in thin-wall AdS3 bubble slices. Geodesic segments satisfy a no-kink matching condition at the wall.
Compute thin-wall Euclidean instanton actions in a dimensionally reduced gravitational description, extremize over bubble radius, and match to probe-brane instanton actions and their flux scaling.

Weinberg's non-Lagrangian construction supplies propagators and external wave functions. The new symmetric multispinor notation simplifies spin sums and traces; amplitudes require all external-leg orientations and the usual fermionic permutation and loop signs.

Tree-level annihilation, Higgs decay, and nucleon-scattering calculations are combined with thermally averaged Boltzmann evolution. Freeze-out and freeze-in are treated separately, with experimental exclusions applied to the resulting mass–coupling parameter space.

Geometric methods use Behrend-weighted Euler characteristics for genus zero, d-critical charts and oriented vanishing-cycle perverse sheaves, followed by pushforward, decomposition and hard Lefschetz to extract spin information.

Construct toric mirrors and Picard–Fuchs periods; integrate trial refined BCOV equations using propagators of weights 1,2,3 and total polynomial degree 3n+3g−3. Conifold gaps, involution symmetry and small-fiber regularity constrain holomorphic ambiguities.

Interpret class II partition functions as twisted-Hilbert-space traces using spin-dependent gradings of rotational fixed points. Test operator products through space-group selection rules, with picture changing when required by vertex-operator ghost charges.

Construct partition functions using Jacobi theta functions and shifted momentum–winding lattice sums. Generate twisted sectors through SL(2,Z) S and T transformations, impose orbifold projections, and check m(L0 − L̄0) ∈ Z, where m is the order of the sector twist.

Extract masses from q and q̄ expansions, impose level matching and orbifold invariance, and estimate the one-loop modular integral using Poisson resummation at large radius and numerical integration at finite radius.

Eliminate an unknown expansion amplitude using a geometric rescaling, then solve a power-law matching condition. In this paper the operation uses the assumed 58 Gly introverse radius, 52 Gly present extroverse radius, and radiation exponent p=1/2.

Normalize kinetic and potential energies by H, change the clock to ln a, and eliminate second derivatives with the background equations. The operation produces a phase-plane system only after the potential-slope evolution is specified.

Use a near-conformal trace anomaly and imported thermal-average expressions for energy density and pressure. Solve the unparticle continuity equation to obtain a(y), then combine it with the Friedmann equations and early- and late-temperature expansions.

Normalize the present density fractions to the paper's adopted Planck values, match B for chosen δ and σ, and constrain the early unparticle-to-radiation ratio using the quoted BBN/CMB bound on additional relativistic energy.

Integrate coupled linear matter and unparticle density-contrast equations with the gravitational potential, using the stated initial conditions. Compare the growth factor, fσ8, and growth index with ΛCDM.

Reduce the exponential-potential background to dimensionless phase-space variables, solve linear perturbations using Bessel/Hankel functions, and apply an Itô Langevin equation near a scaling fixed point. Separate the variance into propagated initial variance and accumulated quantum noise.
Use a curvature–Maxwell coupling for magnetic-field generation, and integral affine quantization with semiclassical phase-space portraits for Brans–Dicke dynamics and frame comparison.
Coarse-grain the scalar field and momentum at a time-dependent comoving cutoff. A Heaviside window produces white noise and Markovian Langevin evolution; this property depends on the window choice.

The single-modulus scan starts with 1,444 combinations over gs∈[10^−3,0.1], Yφ∈[0.01,1], and geometric hierarchy parameter λ∈[10,10^4]. Primordial amplitude and geometry determine W0(V), with W0 restricted to order 1–10^3; abundance matching then fixes V and the DM mass.

Moduli stabilization combines nonperturbative superpotential terms with α′ corrections to the Kähler potential, followed by canonical normalization to obtain masses and decay couplings. Analytical dilution estimates are supplemented by coupled Boltzmann evolution for inflaton, moduli, visible radiation, dark radiation, and DM.

Construct designer models from the modified Friedmann and scalar conservation equations. Because these leave three unknown functions for two equations, specify H as a function of X and determine K(X) and G3X(X).
Isolate the Einstein tensor and ordinary matter, defining κT_DE=G−κT_m. For f(R), metric variation followed by adding and subtracting Gμν provides explicit effective-fluid components.

The authors vary μ and F, integrate until ε=1, and compare N with 60. Captions and prose supply ranges and interpretations, but no solver settings, grid resolution, uncertainty estimates, or tabulated outputs.

The background is closed using an approximate variance rather than a complete interacting-field evolution. The Taylor coefficient and polynomial integration check algebraically, while the fluctuation state, subtraction, and Fourier normalization remain unresolved.

The near-point interaction is restricted by saturating the mass outside the nonadiabatic region. The supplied Figure 3 depicts the resulting flat exterior and central zero. The original production kernel is reused without deriving scattering for this modified profile.

The procedure combines linearization, low-momentum truncation, piecewise frequency approximations, and Airy matching. It assumes short intervals and an adequate background approximation. Interpretation during tachyonic evolution and control of global phase matching remain unresolved.

GRChombo evolves BSSN/CCZ4 equations using fourth-order spatial finite differences and Runge–Kutta time integration, with a moving-puncture gauge. Adaptive refinement is driven by gradients of the metric conformal factor χ.

Initialize at φ(r)=0 with nonzero φ̇(r). The authors argue that vanishing spatial gradients and additional potential terms then preserve the free-field constraint solution. Areal-polar data are converted to conformally flat coordinates and interpolated onto the grid.

Compare evolution with gravity against G=0 evolution on Minkowski space. Falling χ indicates collapse, confirmed by searching for trapped surfaces. Resolution and enlarged-domain checks are reported around changes in outcome.

Expand the probe D8 DBI plus Wess–Zumino action through second order in λ around its interval position. Canonically normalize the adjoint position scalar and gauge fields to identify the force, scalar mass and effective Yang–Mills coupling.

Evaluate a κ-fixed fermionic probe action, reduce a ten-dimensional chiral Majorana spinor to a nine-dimensional Majorana spinor, and introduce non-Abelian couplings through covariantization and a T-duality-required scalar coupling.

Use numerical force profiles and analytic endpoint expansions. For D0 probes, impose Romans-mass tadpole cancellation by attaching F1 strings and include their interval-length energy in the potential.

Rewrite the homogeneous equations as an autonomous system in e-fold time, identify constant-ε scaling solutions, and classify their local stability using eigenvalues of the linearized velocity system. The background treatment explicitly follows earlier scaling-attractor work.

Project covariant linear field perturbations into a local adiabatic/entropic orthonormal basis. Numerically evolve two initially independent mode sets from deep inside the horizon to 60 e-folds after exit, construct their power spectra, and compare superhorizon behavior with neighboring homogeneous 'separate universe' trajectories.

Use the Cuscuton background constraint to express the dynamics through a first-order ODE with φ₀ as a clock. Apply ADM decomposition, choose π-unitary gauge δπ = 0, eliminate lapse, shift and Cuscuton perturbations through constraints, and obtain the quadratic curvature action.

Quantize canonical modes v_k = M_Pzζ_k and u_k = M_Pqδχ_k, with q² = a²F. Numerically solve their oscillator equations and tensor-mode equations, evaluating spectra at pre/post-bounce snapshots. The entropy construction targets q″/q ≈ 2/τ², which yields a Bessel equation and scale-invariant vacuum modes.

Classify symmetry-allowed low-dimension operators, assign adjoint/fundamental large-N factors, and estimate SM loop-induced mixing using momentum-cutoff integrals. Non-renormalizable portal interactions produce quadratically divergent contributions.

Evaluate disk and annulus vertex-operator amplitudes and their low-energy expansions. In the flux-induced mixing amplitude, subtract a factorization pole already represented by axion exchange before identifying the local interaction.

Use Schwinger functionals, a Legendre transform switching Dirichlet to Neumann boundary conditions, and holographic renormalization. Solve quadratic bulk-plus-brane equations with Green functions to obtain current-current interactions.

Expand H=H0+λH1 and solve the perturbed mass-shell equation algebraically. The operator acts as a mass deformation, giving H1=gtt O(p,r,H0,J)/(2H0). At leading PM order this becomes −O(p,r,E,J)/(2E), with the operator evaluated on the Newtonian background.

At leading PM order, Fourier transform the Hamiltonian, discard on-shell terms proportional to p·q at classical order, and transform back. The paper packages this into its Pochhammer replacement rule eliminating J; Appendix A supplies a Fourier-tensor derivation.

For all-PM test-particle results, use a radius transformation r→r+λc(r,H,J), solve differential equations cancelling J dependence, then apply the imported algebraic Hamiltonian-amplitude relation: conserve asymptotic energy to determine local momentum. This replaces explicit loop integration.

Numerically integrate the nonlinear planar PDEs and compare with the reduced single-field equations. The example uses P=X+X²/2, f=e^(2βχ), periodic boundaries, Δx=4×10⁻⁴ and Δt=2×10⁻⁴. The authors report cross-confirmation between independent C and Python/FEniCS implementations.

Expand background and perturbation equations in β⁻¹ and integrate out χ order by order. In spatially flat gauge, eliminate nondynamical lapse and shift using the Faddeev-Jackiw method; also derive a quadratic action for a gauge-invariant density variable through a derivative-dependent variable transformation.

Rewrite P(X) using an auxiliary χ: L=fX−v(f), with v_f=X, f=P_X and v_ff=1/P_XX. A Legendre transformation reconstructs V for a chosen field-space function f; adding χ dynamics gives the linear-kinetic partial completion.

Observer thought experiments compare access to horizon radiation and direct signals. Comoving separation gives an observational-consistency bound; Appendix A uses null trajectories and future-light-cone intersections to argue against information cloning.

Bogoliubov transformations, Fock-state expansions, large-occupation double-factorial asymptotics and polylogarithms estimate non-BD excitation content and its freeze-out time. The extracted quantitative formulas require review.

Separate the potential into VT and ΔV=VX+VH,F+VH,D. Use the semipositive-square structure of the latter terms to motivate their elimination or vanishing. The small-Λ statistical argument scans parameters yielding local minima, including those entering ΔV.

Impose algebraic constrained-superfield conditions: X²=0 removes its scalar; Higgs constraints remove Higgsinos, Higgs auxiliary contributions and half the Higgs scalars; XQ=XL=XWα=0 removes squarks, sleptons and gauginos. Then normalize the surviving fields and minimize the scalar potential.

Differential evolution rounds 484-dimensional real candidate vectors to integer flux matrices. Weighted penalties target eigenvalue, diagonalization, degeneracy, root and tadpole conditions; a subsequent local search changes matrix entries.

Use the Hodge-star-dependent flux potential and its positive semidefiniteness. Minkowski minima require self-dual G4; supersymmetric solutions require primitive (2,2) flux, while nonsupersymmetric Minkowski minima can retain the additional components specified in the text.

For K3 × K3, encode integral flux in a 22 × 22 matrix N and study g = Nd and g̃ = Nᵀd. Spectra and eigenvector signatures determine minima and flat directions; integer norm −2 vectors orthogonal to the positive three-plane diagnose orbifold singularities.

Compare thermal traces with gravitational Euclidean topology sums. For time-translation-preserving saddles on S¹ × Σ, log Z is proportional to β and the leading entropy vanishes. Allowing fillings where the thermal circle contracts produces the black-hole entropy contribution.

Use the QES prescription: extremize generalized entropy Area/(4G) plus bulk von Neumann entropy over appropriately anchored, homologous surfaces, then select the minimum. Entanglement wedge reconstruction supplies the corresponding bulk operator representations.

Partition the reservoir into regions Ri whose individual wedges contain no islands. Locality splits the symmetry operator into a factor on S, factors on Ri, and edge factors. Reconstruction then makes an operator in the collective reservoir island commute with every factor.

Choose a spherical radial gauge in which the sigma-model fields trace an affinely parameterized geodesic. Their constant target-space velocity norm c is the only sigma-model datum entering the reduced Einstein equations.

For a null geodesic, replace τ = 1/r by the multicenter harmonic function Σi ai/|x − xi|. Harmonicity preserves the scalar equations; the chain rule and null target-space tangent make the reduced Einstein source vanish, retaining a flat base.
Write the stationary metric as ds4² = −e^(2U)(dt + AKK)² + e^(−2U)ds3², reduce along the time Killing direction, and dualize the three-dimensional vectors into scalar potentials.

Match chiral-current anomalies across GUT breaking and test effective operators for PQ neutrality. Radiatively induced scalar interactions and effective Majorana operators are used to diagnose symmetry breaking and seesaw compatibility.
Use polar scalar representations, pseudoscalar potentials and mixing matrices to identify the axion by orthogonality to massive pseudoscalars and gauge-boson would-be Goldstones.

Track global and gauged U(1) generators throughout symmetry breaking; construct PQ and B−L as linear combinations that include hypercharge. Derive fermion charges only after fixing scalar charges through the physical Goldstone directions.

Use nonlinear field redefinitions adapted to transformed boundary conditions, then eliminate auxiliary fields and Lagrange-multiplier modes. Further redefinitions decouple the diffeomorphism Stückelberg field from the fermions.
Expand the component action about a bosonic background through third order in all field fluctuations. The imported brane action is expressed in the same conventions before comparing coefficients.

Analyze potential pure cubic Stückelberg contributions using total derivatives, a basis of allowed spinor structures, mass dimensions and supersymmetry variations. This avoids explicitly extending the complete Stückelberg action to third order.

Calculate the non-time-ordered one-loop gravitino self-energy with resummed gauge-boson and gaugino propagators, using bosonic longitudinal/transverse and fermionic spectral densities. Cutting rules relate the loop to production processes.

Numerically integrate the subtracted rate with Cuba while retaining final-state factors 1±fc. The top-Yukawa rate is imported explicitly and depends on λt²[1+At²/(3m3/2²)]; comparison plots use λt=0.7.

Split γ3/2=γsub+γD+γtop. The D-graph contains squared s-, t- and u-channel amplitudes plus thermal 1→2 processes; subtract its scattering contribution from the full squared amplitude to avoid double counting.

Numerically generate helicity-zero modes through the recursion relation and estimate the end-of-inflation energy density from a momentum integral with polarization contractions. Approximate the integral by its upper-end contribution, then apply matter dilution.
Calculate a recoil matrix element using polarization contractions that yield Legendre polynomials; integrate the scattering cross section over halo velocities using the recoil delta function.
Use imported de Sitter Casimir equations with transverse and traceless constraints, a helicity decomposition, Hankel-function mode solutions, and recursion relations for additional tensor components.

Take worldsheet zero modes to obtain a particle action with Hamiltonian constraint h=p²+p̃²+m², diffeomorphism constraint d=p·p̃−M² and a symplectic momentum-mixing term. The energy-scale relation is inferred from the second constraint in the stated zero-momentum limit.

Expand a doubled target-space effective action in the noncommutativity scale, integrate over dual spacetime and use T-duality. The resulting leading action is intensive, expressed as an action-density integral divided by spacetime volume; sequestering is invoked to discuss vacuum-energy stability.

Introduce vector backgrounds by minimal shifts of both momenta. Derive visible/dual mixing from the symplectic term, then motivate scalar and fermion analogues through dimensional reduction, dimensional analysis and free-field supersymmetry.

Reformulates one-variable nilpotent-orbit variation using Nahm equations, charge-compatibility constraints, a Lax formulation and tt* equations. A two-dimensional sigma-model action supplies part of the field equations; charge compatibility must be imposed separately.

Uses convergent near-boundary expansions and operator decompositions under the sl(2) Casimir, weight and charge. Noncommutative recursion constrains expansion coefficients; the finiteness sketch combines these constraints with self-duality, positive norm bounds and flux discreteness.
